title: Pardons Robert Zangrillo
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Robert Zangrillo as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: On May 24, 2018, President Donald Trump granted Robert Zangrillo a presidential pardon. The supplied Department of Justice clemency listing associates Zangrillo with federal fraud, bribery, and money-laundering offenses, but lists no sentence. Trump pardoned Robert Zangrillo on May 24, 2018. The case involved allegations of mail and wire fraud, honest-services fraud, federal-program bribery, and money laundering in Massachusetts. The clemency listing gives no sentence or final case disposition, so the pardon’s practical effect and stated rationale remain unknown.
description_long: Trump’s May 24, 2018 pardon of Robert Zangrillo is the event recorded here. The Justice Department’s clemency list names the District of Massachusetts and lists conspiracy involving mail and wire fraud, honest-services fraud, federal-program bribery, and money laundering, as well as related counts. The same listing reports no sentence. The available material therefore supports identifying the pardon and the allegations or offenses named in the record, but it does not explain what judgment, if any, had been entered by the time of the pardon, what conduct was admitted or contested, or why clemency was granted. Those details matter to a fuller account of the case and the pardon’s practical effect. Until the case disposition and the pardon’s stated rationale are supplied, this description should not characterize Zangrillo’s guilt, the resolution of the charges, or any political connection.

The Justice Department listing names an indictment in the Southern District of New York involving alleged fraud and money laundering, and says the case had no further resolution in the listing. The supplied information does not explain the pardon’s scope or how it affected the pending charges.
description_long: The supplied entry identifies a January 19, 2021 pardon for Tommaso Buti. The Justice Department’s clemency list gives no sentence and describes an indictment in the Southern District of New York involving alleged wire fraud, a scheme concerning money and state tax stamps, and money-laundering conspiracy. title: Pardons Abel Holtz
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Abel Holtz as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: On January 19, 2021, Trump pardoned Abel Holtz. The Justice Department lists a Southern District of Florida conviction for obstruction of justice, with 45 days’ imprisonment, two years of supervised release, and a $20,000 fine. The entry notes that the sentence was amended. The available record does not provide the president’s rationale for granting clemency.
description_long: Abel Holtz’s pardon was among Trump’s final clemency actions, issued on January 19, 2021. The Justice Department lists Holtz’s case in the Southern District of Florida and identifies obstruction of justice as the offense. It records a 45-day prison term, two years of supervised release with conditions, and a $20,000 fine, noting that the sentence was amended. Holtz’s sentence included a short prison term, supervised release, and a fine, while the clemency announcement gave no reason for the pardon. The entry does not state why Trump selected Holtz for clemency, what arguments were made in support of the request, or whether every financial condition was affected. The documented event is the presidential pardon of a person with an obstruction conviction and a short custodial sentence. Any explanation of motive or political significance would require evidence beyond the details provided in the linked federal list.

title: Commutes Sentence of Corvain T. Cooper
description_short: Trump commuted the sentence of Corvain T. Cooper as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: On January 19, 2021, Trump commuted Corvain T. Cooper’s sentence. The Justice Department identifies a life sentence for marijuana-trafficking conspiracy and related money-laundering offenses in the Western District of North Carolina. The supplied list establishes the conviction and original sentence but does not identify the new term or release conditions created by the commutation.
description_long: Corvain T. Cooper received a presidential commutation on January 19, 2021, according to the supplied entry. The Justice Department lists a Western District of North Carolina conviction for conspiring to possess marijuana with intent to distribute, conspiring to commit money laundering, and structuring currency transactions. It records a life sentence followed by supervised release. That severe sentence is key background, but the source material reviewed here does not state the replacement term or whether Cooper was released immediately. A commutation changes the sentence while leaving the conviction in place; without the actual warrant or updated sentence, the practical result cannot be stated precisely. The missing context is the commuted term, any release date or supervision conditions, and the administration’s stated reason for selecting Cooper. The new term and release conditions would determine whether the action shortened Cooper’s custody or altered supervision.
